>

>
> > Or are the damage from Outside the Hourglass considered to be dealt at

Because the range is close when OtH deals damage, and when the range is set to long it is too late to trigger the Improvised flamethrower? Please folks, stop confounding what is happening. There is no LIFO queue. A card is played. It resolves. Play the next card, or pass the impulse. Rinse, repeat.

In the order described, OtH first, the damage is done at default range (close). Then Silence sets the range to long, Alpha Glint ends combat...all in that order. The 2 damage event happened at close range.

Reverse the SS and OtH and you get ranged damage. Likewise, if you do that at a minion with an Imp Flamethrower, you get the ImpFT explosion effect, cause the range was at long range.

If you OtH and then maneuver in the "Set Range Step", OtH damage has ALREADY happened, at predefined conditions (close).

The only question that really exist is if Disarm and Pulled Fangs, which lack "Only playable at close range" are indeed really playable at long, if you managed to pull of prerange damage at close.

For that, we need Pascal.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
Here's a quick list of the rulings:
OtH stands for Outside the Hourglass
Unless written, no other cards are played. Cards are played in the order they are written (from left to right)

- OtH + Majesty + Disarm => Valid.
- OtH + Maneuver to long + Majesty Disarm => Not valid.
- OtH + Alpha Glint + Disram => Valid.
- OtH + Selective Silence + Disarm => Not valid.
- Selective Silence + OtH + Disarm => Not valid.
- OtH + Fear of the Void Below + Majesty + Disarm => Valid.
- Fear of the Void Below + OtH + Majesty + Disarm => Not valid
- OtH when opposing has a Improvised Flamethrower + Maneveur/set range to long => Improvised Flamethrower does not explode.

Basically, Disarm isn't playable at long range (all the Disarm points), and damage is resolved when it is inflicted - we don't retro-check it (last point).

I'm under the impression that slightly changing Disarm from this:
>
> Only usable at the end of a round of combat in which this vampire successfully inflicted more damage at close range than the opposing vampire.
>
to this:
>
> Only usable at close range at the end of a round of combat in which this vampire successfully inflicted more damage than the opposing vampire.
>
would be enough. Pulled Fangs would follow the same pattern.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
A possible clarification in the rules would be:

> 6.4.2. Determine Range
>
> Each round of combat is fought at either close range or long range. Close range is the default for each round. The range determines which strikes and other strike-resolution-phase effects can be used. Some effects can only be used at close range, some only at long range, and some at either close or long range (see below). Once the range has been determined, it applies to the whole round (including effects that have happened before range has been determined, such as damage that would have been dealt during the round before the Determine Range step).
>
Though not necessary, this wouldn't prevent Disarm and Pulled Fangs from being reworded for clarity.

Regarding interaction with Improvised Flamethrower, nothing is retroactive in the game so there's no issue here, merely a possible clarification.

Prince of Paris, France
